The issue, in full:

What happens: reference-harness/browser/engines/ts-server.mjs serves the mods' public files (TinyMCE's theme, the ace modes, the style images) from DECKO_MOD_PUBLIC_DIR, which defaults to reference-harness/oracle/app/public, and refuses to boot without its mod/ directory ('DECKO_MOD_PUBLIC_DIR has no mod/ directory'). items.title: The treewalk rig reads a citation of a different Ruby file as a claim about the row's Ruby (bare leaf names in the source set are unique in the row, not in the deck)
items.assignment:
Fix GitHub issue 42 in KatsuJinCode/decko-ts: "The treewalk rig reads a citation of a different Ruby file as a claim about the row's Ruby (bare leaf names in the source set are unique in the row, not in the deck)".

Work in /data/home/decko-ts, from origin/deploy/full-candidate-20261104 (the port's working line; main is the old work board). Read its AGENTS.md first and follow it. Touch only your own branch; other agents work on other branches. Nothing is ever sent or shown to anyone outside this repository.

The issue, in full:

The register-treewalk rig reads a port file's citation of a DIFFERENT Ruby file as a claim about this row's Ruby, because the row's source set carries bare leaf names.

WHAT THE RIG PROMISES. `tools/treewalk-family-ruby-file-set.mjs` (rowRubySources) says:

    // A bare name joins the source set only when this row's own file set is
    // the only place in the deck with that name.

and then checks the row's OWN file set:

    for (const [leaf, owners] of baseNames) {
      if (owners.length === 1) sources.add(leaf);
    }

So for the row `reg-treewalk-c2-name-rb-name-all-all-descendants-all-parts-card-cl` the source set carries the bare leaves `all.rb`, `name.rb`, `parts.rb`, `descendants.rb`, `card_class.rb` and `name_variants.rb`, because those leaves are unique among the row's six files. They are NOT unique in the deck: `card-1.110.0/lib/card/rule/all.rb`, `card-1.110.0/lib/card/director/card_class.rb` and others carry the same leaf names.

WHAT THE MATCH THEN DOES. `tools/treewalk-family-row-disposition.mjs` matches a citation against the row's sources with:

    c.rubySource === s || c.rubySource.endsWith(`/${s}`) || s.endsWith(`/${c.rubySource}`)

so a port file that cites `lib/card/rule/all.rb` matches the row's bare `all.rb`, and a file that cites `lib/card/director/card_class.rb` matches the row's bare `card_class.rb`. A citation of a file that is NOT part of the row is then read as the port's own claim about that row's Ruby.

WHAT IT COSTS. Measured on 2026-10-27 while working the name row: three of the row's defs (update_superleft, superize_name and field_names) were written as NAMED-COLLAPSE statements, and the rig measured all three as PORTED-INLINE instead, with the citation recorded as `lib/card/rule/all.rb` and `lib/card/director/card_class.rb`, which are different Ruby files. The receipt and the fixture would have carried a citation of the wrong Ruby file. The fix in the lane was to write the claim so the rig read it as a collapse, and the receipt names the real carriers; the instrument itself still mis-matches.

THE FIX. The bare leaf belongs in the source set only when it is unique in the DECK, not in the row. The deck's file list is available to the resolver (the pinned gemset is indexed by the same tool), so the guard can be measured the way its own comment describes. A bare leaf that is ambiguous in the deck should either be dropped from the source set or be matched against the row's full paths only, so a citation of `lib/card/rule/all.rb` never stands in for `name/all.rb`.

MEASURED ON THE TREE AS IT STANDS. The row reads GAP 0 either way (the rig's dispositions for the name row are PORTED 27 / PORTED-INLINE 22 / NAMED-COLLAPSE 2 / SKIP 4), so this is about the rig's honesty about WHICH Ruby a citation names, not about the row's verdict.

items.title: A read-rule rewrite that only swaps the rule content does not take effect until the next engine boot (stale in-process read-rule grant)
items.assignment:
Fix GitHub issue 41 in KatsuJinCode/decko-ts: "A read-rule rewrite that only swaps the rule content does not take effect until the next engine boot (stale in-process read-rule grant)".

Work in /data/home/decko-ts, from origin/deploy/full-candidate-20261104 (the port's working line; main is the old work board). Read its AGENTS.md first and follow it. Touch only your own branch; other agents work on other branches. Nothing is ever sent or shown to anyone outside this repository.

The issue, in full:

Measured 2026-10-27 on the demo scratch deck (sqlite staging server, DECKO_WRITE_PATH=1).

**What happened**

79 junction cards (Class X+Video Player) carried a public read rule. A maintenance pass rewrote each rule card content from [[Anyone]] to [[Anyone Signed In]] through the write path (PUT Class X+Video Player+*self+*read, HTTP 303), then probed the card signed out. Every probe kept answering 200 with the card body for minutes - through the measured rule-binding settle window, through a re-write cycle, and on manual re-probes 10 minutes later. Storage was already correct the whole time: the rule card row held content [[Anyone Signed In]], its card_references row pointed referee anyone_signed_in (id 9), and the junction row pointed read_rule_id at that rule card. One process restart later the same probe answered 403 on all 79 junctions with no further writes.

**Mechanism as measured**

The serving process granted the read from stale in-process state: the deck-wide read-rule grant map built from rule cards joined to card_references (the ReadRuleCache shape in src/card/permissions/read-rules.ts) kept serving the pre-rewrite grant for those rule ids after the rule CONTENT and its reference rows changed. A rule-id-level invalidation exists for rule card creation (the settle lag measured 2026-10-26 bound within seconds), but a content-only rewrite of an existing rule card left the old grant live until reboot. The same rewrite shape on cards whose rule was created in an earlier process lifetime (Library Row junctions) denied correctly - the difference is which side of the cache the rewrite landed on, not the card shape: both sets of rows were byte-identical in structure when compared directly in sqlite.

**Why it matters**

A retire/deny pass that re-points an existing public rule to Anyone Signed In looks successful in storage but keeps serving the card to signed-out visitors until someone reboots the engine. The demo decks behind the family gate run write-armed; any lane doing a security-relevant rule tightening through the write path gets a false FAIL (or worse, a false PASS on the stored state while the surface leaks) depending on cache history.

**Reproduction**

1. Boot a deck; make sure rule card R exists with content [[Anyone]] and card C points at it (read_rule_id=R).
2. Signed out, GET C -> 200.
3. PUT R with content [[Anyone Signed In]]; wait; confirm storage: R content, R references, C.read_rule_id all correct.
4. Signed out, GET C -> still 200 (expected: 403).
5. Restart the process; signed out, GET C -> 403.

**Suggested direction**

Invalidate (or recompute) the in-memory grant entry for a rule card id when that card's content or reference rows change on the write path - the same hook that makes freshly created rule cards bind within the measured settle window.

items.assignment:
Fix GitHub issue 40 in KatsuJinCode/decko-ts: "The edge host's asset-input refresh publishes asset inputs whose bytes reference vendored mod files the port does not serve, so the served stylesheet breaks a page asset".

Work in /data/home/decko-ts, from origin/deploy/full-candidate-20261104 (the port's working line; main is the old work board). Read its AGENTS.md first and follow it. Touch only your own branch; other agents work on other branches. Nothing is ever sent or shown to anyone outside this repository.

The issue, in full:

What happened: with the edge serving host's asset-input refresh seam wired (the register-routes B6 row's own unblock, the edge-refresh-seam lane), the whole-family signed-in exercise's final browser asset audit fails: GET /mod/style/jquery-ui-smoothness/ui-bg_glass_65_ffffff_1x400.png answers 404, and the run reads 331 of 332 checks (the base tree passes the same audit).

The mechanism, measured on the rolled tree with the seam wired: the seam runs Ruby's Card::Assets.refresh before the card GETs, and the refresh publishes the deck's asset inputs from the port's vendored mod sources - the local deck's card_virtuals rows carry the run's own timestamps and the stylesheet the browser loaded is the refresh's published bytes (the deck's slate_skin_customized output, 365,147 bytes, served at /files/45514/320151191367.css). That published stylesheet references the jQuery UI theme's image files under /mod/style/jquery-ui-smoothness/ (14 of them). The port's vendored style snapshot carries the theme's CSS and SCSS and none of its image files (0 PNGs under fixtures/vendor/mod-style-assets, and no copy of that image anywhere in the tree), and the port serves no mod asset of its own: the edge host's vendor-asset arm answers the FontAwesome and bootstrap-font paths only (deploy/bunny-worker-src/bunny-edge-engine-handler.ts, serveFontAwesomeAsset / serveBootstrapFontAsset). So the image the published stylesheet asks for answers 404.

How it could be better: two ways out, and the port owns both. (1) The refresh should publish the deck's stored asset-input bytes rather than a re-compilation whose image references the port cannot serve; the port's own assembly of the skin is byte-pinned to Ruby's bytes (tests/card/assets/skin-stylesheet.test.ts, 'the slate skin compiles to Ruby's stylesheet'), so the divergence is in what the refresh publishes for the deck's customized skin, not in the compiler. (2) The port should serve the mods' vendored files the way the original does, and the vendored style snapshot should carry the theme's image files (they ship with the gem; the snapshot has the CSS and the SCSS and none of the images).

Evidence: the failing leg's evidence JSON in the run record of the rolled tree (.runtime of the roll v14 exercise run, 'final browser asset audit / no script, stylesheet, font or image failed across the exercised browser contexts') names the one 404 and 38 contexts; the local deck's card_virtuals rows read the run's own timestamps and the served stylesheet's bytes are the refresh's published output; fixtures/vendor/mod-style-assets holds 0 PNGs. items.title: The whole-family exercise's local stack intermittently stops answering the browser, aborting the gate with a timeout instead of the stack's state
items.assignment:
Fix GitHub issue 39 in KatsuJinCode/decko-ts: "The whole-family exercise's local stack intermittently stops answering the browser, aborting the gate with a timeout instead of the stack's state".

Work in /data/home/decko-ts, from origin/deploy/full-candidate-20261104 (the port's working line; main is the old work board). Read its AGENTS.md first and follow it. Touch only your own branch; other agents work on other branches. Nothing is ever sent or shown to anyone outside this repository.

The issue, in full:

## What happened

The whole-family signed-in exercise (`tools/edge-signed-in-exercise.mjs`) drives a local stack over a copy of the pinned deck. Three runs of the same command at the same tree (`aba86c7a4`, source files clean, the same bundle SHA-256 `0760c857b5807eccae3066e99b3bd4762b930237ff221c92e5d1f07b4b3ce7b2`) on 2026-10-26 behaved like this:

| run | result | what stopped it |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 241 of 244 checks, then abort | the stack stopped answering the browser: `page.goto` timed out after 30 s on a card page in the delete-edit-race module, then the fixture was quarantined and the remaining modules never ran |
| 2 | 74 of 75 checks, then abort | the stack stopped answering the browser: `page.goto` timed out after 60 s on the sign-in page in the account module |
| 3 | 332 of 332 checks | nothing; this run had the machine to itself |

The stack was not slow before it stopped: run 2's slowest own-work request reads 1037 ms of server time and run 1's reads 2246 ms, against 4731 ms in a run that completed. The hang is a stall, not a slow page. The exercise's own request log for the aborted runs shows only the usual aborted navigations, and the stack's own stderr is not recorded, so the mechanism is not established from the run records.

## What it cost

Two of the three runs of the family gate produced a grade that could not be compared with anything (the abort leaves the capabilities of the modules that never ran reading not covered), so the lane that owns the roll could not read the family grade at the tip and had to re-run the exercise before it could close the roster rows. The third run, on an idle machine, read the full 332 of 332.

## How it could be better

The stack's stderr and its in-process worker state belong in the run record, so a stall leaves evidence instead of only a browser timeout. The exercise's own rule that a run reports the checks it graded, and not the ones it never reached, is right; what is missing is the reason it stopped.

Two things would make the next stall diagnosable and the gate usable:

- the local stack's stderr, and the worker's state at the moment the browser gave up, written next to the run record;
- the harness's own decision about a stalled stack: a request that never answers should end the run with the stack's state named, not with a browser timeout and a quarantined fixture.

The frequency also matters: this is the gate every roll depends on, and it now aborts some runs on a busy machine. Whether the stall is the stack's own, the deck walk's (the run's deck serves by walking its nest closure, the index version reads none), or the machine's load is not established yet, and the first step is to record the stack's own state when it stops.

items.title: The P5 capability leg's fixture names meet the engine's inflection: a stamp ending in s makes the leg read an empty set key list
items.assignment:
Fix GitHub issue 38 in KatsuJinCode/decko-ts: "The P5 capability leg's fixture names meet the engine's inflection: a stamp ending in s makes the leg read an empty set key list".

Work in /data/home/decko-ts, from origin/deploy/full-candidate-20261104 (the port's working line; main is the old work board). Read its AGENTS.md first and follow it. Touch only your own branch; other agents work on other branches. Nothing is ever sent or shown to anyone outside this repository.

The issue, in full:

## What happened

The `caps-legs` module's P5 leg (`P5 *type_plus_right Set: a +*type_plus_right+*structure rule renders for members and not outside the set`, `tools/edge-signed-in-exercise/checks-capability-legs.mjs`) reads its verdict from the visited card's own set keys, and it names its fixture cards with the run's own millisecond stamp:

    const name = (label) => `Harness_Leg_${label}_${Date.now().toString(36)}`;

Every card of that leg therefore shares one stamp, and one base36 character of that stamp decides whether the leg can read its own evidence.

The engine computes a card's key through the ActiveSupport inflection tables (`src/card/name/inflect.ts`), whose default singular rule strips a trailing `s`. When the stamp ends in `s`, the card's key is the name without that `s`, while the leg's anchor comparison (`cardAnchors` in `tools/edge-signed-in-exercise/lib/rule-set-legs.mjs`) lowercases the raw name. The two never meet, the leg finds no slot whose SELF, RIGHT or TYPE_PLUS_RIGHT token names the card, and it records an empty set key list.

Measured on 2026-10-26 at the rolled candidate tip `aba86c7a4`: a run whose stamp was `mvq2bjas` recorded the leg FAIL with `"setKeys":[]`, `"typePlusRightToken":null`, while `"showsHeader":true`. The captured page of that run carries the rule's own header and the token `TYPE_PLUS_RIGHT-rich_text-harness_leg_tpright_mvq2bja`, so the engine answered correctly and the rule's set was the card's set; only the leg's key comparison failed. The runs whose stamp does not end in `s` read the same leg PASS with the full token list.

## What it cost

One whole-family exercise run in three aborted at 241 of 332 checks with that leg red, on a tree whose residual fix for that leg had already landed and was correct. The failure probability is one base36 character in thirty-six per run, so it reaches roughly one run in a year of daily gates, and when it does it is indistinguishable from a real regression of the lane's fix. A lane that reads the red leg has to re-run the whole exercise to find out whether the tree or the clock is at fault.

## How it could be better

The leg must not depend on the last character of its own fixture names. Either

- the fixture names end in a character the inflection tables leave alone (for example a letter the default singular rules do not match, or a fixed suffix after the stamp), or
- the anchor comparison resolves a name through the same inflection tables the engine uses (the card's key, not the raw lowercased name), which is the fix that keeps the leg honest for any deck.

The second one is the better repair: the deck may amend its own inflection tables at boot (`applyDeckInflections` in `src/card/name/inflect.ts`), so a leg that reads the raw name can miss the card's real key on any deck whose tables differ from the defaults.

The same class of defect should be checked in the other capability legs that name their fixture cards with a timestamp (`Harness_Leg_*` and `Harness_CB_*`).

The issue, in full:

WHAT: `node tools/treewalk-family-row-disposition.mjs --all --json` measures the register-treewalk family's thirty rows in one pass. It is the input of `tools/treewalk-family-row-receipts.mjs` (the family's receipt generator, which writes every row's RECEIPT.md and the family's index) and of the pinned capture `tests/server/oracle-capture-card-gem-row-methods-ruby.rb`, which reads the same tool. On this tree the whole-family pass takes more than 30 minutes, while one row takes about 20 seconds.

MEASURED (2026-10-25, branch port/treewalk-format-20261026, tip 72688b629, Windows, node v24.22.1):

- one row (`reg-treewalk-c2-format-rb-format-content-context-names-render-regi`, 8 Ruby files, 76 defs): 19.5 s, measured with `time node tools/treewalk-family-row-disposition.mjs <row-id> --json`.
- the whole family (30 rows): still running after 30 minutes. Two earlier runs were killed at 900 s and at about 2100 s without finishing, and `tools/treewalk-family-row-receipts.mjs` failed the same way: its inner `--all` call was killed at 900 s and the receipt generator exited non-zero with "Command failed: node tools/treewalk-family-row-disposition.mjs --all --json".

WHY IT IS SLOW: the gemset side is indexed once (the tool says so in its own header), but the port side is not. For every def the tool scans the whole port tree's citation set three times: the line-range-map search, the cited-method candidate search, and the collapse-sentence search. Each of those is a full pass over every citation in every port file, so the family run costs (the family's total def count) times (the port tree's citation count), with the per-def constant around 0.26 s.

The per-def file READS were fixed once already (the tool's comment: "re-reading every port file per def made the family run take minutes"). The scans over the citation index that the tool already builds are the part that is still per def.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT: index the port citations once, by cited method name and by ruby source, and index the collapse sentences by the method names they name, so a def's three lookups are lookups rather than full scans. The disposition rules do not have to change. The output must stay identical, and the per-row fixtures under `fixtures/captured/` are the check: `tests/server/treewalk-row-disposition-parity.test.ts` compares each fixture with the rig's current output for that row, so a changed output fails there.

A receipt step that takes half an hour, and that times out at fifteen minutes, is the difference between a lane landing its receipt and a lane giving up on it. items.title: Treewalk rig: the citation matcher reads another gem's file as this row's, and the collapse rule drops its own line-range check
items.assignment:
Fix GitHub issue 29 in KatsuJinCode/decko-ts: "Treewalk rig: the citation matcher reads another gem's file as this row's, and the collapse rule drops its own line-range check".

Work in /data/home/decko-ts, from origin/deploy/full-candidate-20261104 (the port's working line; main is the old work board). Read its AGENTS.md first and follow it. Touch only your own branch; other agents work on other branches. Nothing is ever sent or shown to anyone outside this repository.

The issue, in full:

What happened: while closing `reg-treewalk-c2-director-rb-director-rb-9` (branch `port/treewalk-director-20261026`), four of the row's eleven `director.rb` methods carry a label that rests on a name-level match with ANOTHER gem's file, and the rig's collapse rule reads a sentence about a different method as this row's collapse.

## Facet 1: the citation matcher is looser than the rule it states

`tools/treewalk-family-ruby-file-set.mjs:206-226` builds the row's source list and adds the bare leaf of every file (`director/all.rb` contributes `all.rb`). The disposition matcher (`tools/treewalk-family-row-disposition.mjs:697-706`, `:741-748`, `:785-794`, `:856-862`, `:877-887`, `:986-991`) then accepts a citation when `c.rubySource.endsWith('/' + s)`, so a citation of ANY path ending in the row's leaf counts as a citation of the row's file. The resolver's own rule (`:200-205`) says a bare citation counts only when the leaf is unique to the row: the row's own file set is what makes `all.rb` unique, not the deck.

Measured on the director row at `34669fccf`:

- `main?` (`director.rb:160`) is PORTED through `card/mod-loader/mods/card-mod-history.ts:1907`, a `const main` binding whose file cites `set/event/all.rb`.
- `head?` (`director.rb:164`) is PORTED through `card/render/head-views.ts:87`, whose file cites `set/all/head.rb`.
- `register` (`director.rb:168`) is PORTED-INLINE through `card/set-patterns/registry.ts:15`, whose file cites `lib/card/set/pattern/class_methods.rb#register`, another gem's file with the row's `class_methods.rb` leaf.

None of the three labels would survive a matcher that requires the citation to name the row's own path.

## Facet 2: the collapse rule computes the check it describes and never applies it

`:961` builds `range` and `:971` builds `covers` ("the method's line must fall inside ONE of the sentence's line references, and the reference must name this row's Ruby file"), and neither is read afterwards: `:983-991` test only the whole-word name and the file's citations. So a sentence about a DIFFERENT method that shares the name is read as this row's collapse: the director row's `delete` (`director.rb:176`) is classified NAMED-COLLAPSE by the engine's subcards sentence "a posted trash arm routes to the delete path (trashInWriter)", which is about `subcards/all.rb`'s `drop_field`.

## What it cost

A row's grade is a number a reader cannot check, because four of its labels rest on a citation of another gem's file. The receipt that carries those labels has to explain the coincidence in prose, and the row's own numbers would change under a corrected matcher.

## Suggested fix direction

1. Match a citation against the row's own paths at SEGMENT boundaries: the gem-relative path, the path without the gem, or a suffix of it. Admit the bare leaf only when it is unique in the row.
2. Apply the `covers` check the rule already states, so a collapse sentence must cite a line range covering the method's own line in the row's own file.

Then re-measure the family in one pass: every row's labels move, so the change belongs to the family lane, not to one row's lane. This is the same rig as #27 (the mention-index facet); the two facets should land in one re-measurement.

## Reproduction

Add a port-file comment citing another gem's file whose leaf matches a row file (`set/event/all.rb` for a row whose file set holds `director/all.rb`), name one of the row's defs in that file, and re-run `node tools/treewalk-family-row-disposition.mjs <row-id>`: the def is classified from that citation.
